title: Report on Mouse Disappearance When Zooming Out While Enabling Zoom LT Screen Recording

judgment.rationale: The report already gives a concrete Zoom LT + recording + disable-live-zoom sequence, and current ZoomIt source explicitly toggles cursor-capture behavior when live zoom enters or leaves annotation mode, so a maintainer-side reproduce/trace pass is the next useful step.
evidence: The issue body describes a five-step repro: start Zoom LT recording support, begin recording, activate the zooming function, then disable it and observe the mouse pointer disappear.
The actual behavior is precise: the pointer becomes visually invisible while recording continues.
`src/modules/ZoomIt/ZoomIt/MirrorWindow.cpp` explicitly enables/disables cursor capture based on `AnnotationState::AnnotatingLiveZoom`, which matches the reported on/off zoom transition.
There are no follow-up comments or linked fixes that would make more reporter clarification more valuable than an internal reproduction trace.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the cursor-loss transition while toggling Zoom LT during recording and trace whether cursor capture is restored correctly when live zoom exits.

fix_assessment.rationale: The source exposes a plausible cursor-capture path, but reproduction should confirm whether the failure belongs to ZoomIt live-zoom state, Windows Graphics Capture, or recorder interaction before proposing code changes.

issue_context.summary: ZoomIt's live zoom can reportedly hide the mouse pointer when the user disables zoom during an active recording session. The public repro is already concrete enough for a maintainer-side reproduction pass.
known_information: The report targets ZoomIt on PowerToys 0.100.2 from the Microsoft Store on Windows 11 23H2.
The reporter says the issue occurs with both the built-in Windows screen recorder and QQ's recording feature.
The sequence is specific: recording is already running, live zoom is turned on, then turning live zoom off makes the cursor disappear.
There are no public comments, bug-report ZIPs, or linked pull requests on the issue.
inferences: This is more likely a state transition problem around live zoom cursor rendering/capture than a generic recorder startup failure.
Because the report already isolates the transition, another generic reporter questionnaire would add less value than direct internal reproduction.
issue_context.analysis: The public issue is already narrow: it names the module, trigger, and visible failure. Source review shows that MirrorWindow changes cursor-capture behavior when `AnnotatingLiveZoom` toggles, which makes this a good candidate for a reproduce-first triage action instead of a request for more logs.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the full issue body and confirmed there are no public follow-up comments or linked fixes.
Inspected `src/modules/ZoomIt/ZoomIt/MirrorWindow.cpp` and confirmed `EnableCursorCapture(...)` is toggled when live zoom enters or leaves annotation mode.

Inspected the recording entry points in `src/modules/ZoomIt/ZoomIt/Zoomit.cpp` and confirmed recording and mirroring are coordinated but still use explicit state transitions worth tracing during the reported zoom-off step.

actions.label: Reproduce Zoom LT cursor loss while recording
actions.note: Validate whether cursor capture is restored correctly when live zoom is disabled mid-recording.

reproduce.version_requirement: PowerToys 0.100.2 or a nearby build with Zoom LT/live zoom and screen recording available.
prerequisites: A Windows machine where ZoomIt live zoom works normally.
A recording path that shows the issue, such as the built-in Windows recorder or QQ recorder.
steps: Start a recording session using the same recorder type the reporter described.
Enable Zoom LT/live zoom while the recording is already in progress.
Disable Zoom LT/live zoom again using the same button or shortcut used to toggle it.
Observe whether the cursor remains visible locally and in the captured recording, then repeat once without recording as a control case.
reproduce.expected_result: Disabling live zoom during recording should restore the normal visible cursor instead of making it disappear.
